chapter: Ellington band: drinking, quarrels and rent parties
title: Ivie Anderson, Cootie Williams and the gun in El Paso
summary: Cootie hit Ivie Anderson in the head with a window jack during a train card game; she bought a gun in El Paso, but Duke cooled it and the two ended up together.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: We was on the train once and they were gambling, and Ivie Anderson was in the game. So she was always lucky. She'd win. But she did something to Cootie, so -- remember those old things they used to raise the windows up? They had to put it under something and jack it up, like to raise it up? -- so Cootie took one of them things and just looked at her, bam, hit her right in the head. And she had a big gash.

So now she's going to kill Cootie. So the train stopped in El Paso, Texas, and it stays there for a while, you know, and she got off there and she went and bought a gun somewhere. She came back, and I told Cootie, 'Cool it.' I said, 'I think she's got something in that bag.' He said,

Then Duke was talking to Ivie. He said, "Let him alone and don't bother him because he might kill you." So I don't know how they cooled it off some kind of way and the first thing you know Ivie and Cootie was going together.
